passages.provision_quote: (4) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2025, three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%).
passages.note: Section 4 cuts the individual income tax rate from 3.23% to 3.15%, but the same 'various tax matters' act also repeals the utility receipts tax and adds an unrelated Medicaid managed-care reporting directive, so this is one clause of an omnibus, not a single-subject bill.

Senate Roll Call 374 passed the HB 1002 conference committee report 50 Yea to 0 Nay; Mishler is named as the bill's mover and listed among the Yea votes, but a vote with 0% opposition cannot alone establish a chair.
passages.actor_quote: Bray Ford Jon Mishler Walker K

passages.note: Mishler is listed as a Senate sponsor of HB 1002, whose own digest describes several distinct provisions (an income tax rate cut, a mini-mill property tax valuation election, repeal of the utility receipts tax), confirming the bill bundles multiple tax matters rather than one clause.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Ryan Mishler, Sen. Travis Holdman, Sen. Lonnie Randolph.

rows.reasoning: HB 1002 (2022) cuts the individual income tax rate from 3.23% to 3.15% and repeals the utility receipts tax, but the same 'various tax matters' act bundles in unrelated provisions (a mini-mill property tax valuation election, a Medicaid managed-care reporting directive), so it is multi-subject. Mishler's Senate sponsorship and his 50-0 vote for the conference committee report show a tax-cutting direction but, with no vote tally above near-unanimous and no statement of his tying the act to the rate-cut clause specifically, do not establish whether 'Cut taxes broadly, including the main rates most people pay' versus another rung is intended.
